instruction: Every time I open Chrome, it loads my previous tabs. I'd prefer it to just open a new tab page instead. Please configure Chrome to open the New Tab page on startup.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt install jq -y
cd /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && jq '. + {"session":{"restore_on_startup":1}}' Preferences > temp && mv temp Preferences

metadata.explanation: This task requires changing Chrome's startup behavior from 'Continue where you left off' (restore_on_startup=1) to 'Open the New Tab page' (restore_on_startup=5). The setup configures Chrome with restore_on_startup=1. The custom getter checks if Chrome is set to open New Tab page and returns 'true' or 'false'. The custom metric performs exact match comparison.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the instruction requirement: Chrome configured to open New Tab page on startup
Getter logic is correct: reads Chrome Preferences file and checks restore_on_startup setting (5=New Tab, 1=Continue where left off)
Getter correctly handles edge case where session key doesn't exist (defaults to New Tab)
Metric logic is correct: performs exact match comparison between result and expected value
Expected value is semantically correct: 'true' when restore_on_startup=5 or session key is missing
Data flow is sound: getter extracts right state -> returns 'true'/'false' -> metric compares -> expected='true'
State is accessible and persistent: Chrome Preferences file is stable, no postconfig needed
Complete coverage: evaluator checks the only requirement in the instruction
Cross-platform support: handles Windows, macOS, and Linux file paths correctly
Error handling is present: catches exceptions during file read and returns 'false' as fallback
